messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] MethylKit methSeg() error: all(segMedianT == 0)
parts:
Trial and error - had to set the segMedianT in to the command. By specifying -100,100 (max and min for methylation difference) I got methSeg to run.

methSeg(gr.methDiff.42453, diagnostic.plot=TRUE, maxInt=40, minSeq=10, segMedianT=-100,100)

But my questions is then, how would I determine the signifigance in this case if I'm giving the tresholds rather than letting methSeg to determine them? Or does it mean that there aren't any significant segments in my data as methSeg cannot determine the segMedianT on it's own?

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] MethylKit methSeg() error: all(segMedianT == 0)
parts: You need to create a GRanges object that has one numeric column that contains the methylation difference. You can filter your data to contain only DMCs with a certain qvalue threshold, and run segmentation on that
On Tue, 7 Mar 2017 at 06:34, Heidi Viitaniemi <hmv...@gmail.com> wrote:

Trial and error - had to set the segMedianT in to the command. By specifying -100,100 (max and min for methylation difference) I got methSeg to run.

methSeg(gr.methDiff.42453, diagnostic.plot=TRUE, maxInt=40, minSeq=10, segMedianT=-100,100)

But my questions is then, how would I determine the signifigance in this case if I'm giving the tresholds rather than letting methSeg to determine them? Or does it mean that there aren't any significant segments in my data as methSeg cannot determine the segMedianT on it's own?

messages.author: 9c69ed22aa4df507
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] MethylKit methSeg() error: all(segMedianT == 0)
parts:
Thanks Altuna for your prompt response!

I was able to reproduce the p-value issue with the methylKit example dataset as well. Attached is what I ran. My own data is 63 files so that is why I've been using the methylDB objects.

For me exporting the data as(xx, "methylDiff") output p-values for both regression and Fisher objects. But if I try transform the mehtylDiff to GRanges then the p-value is not output. With this I realised that the myDiff object from Fisher analysis is actually a methylDiff (not methylDB as the outpur from regression). So as(methylDiffDB, "Granges") outputs both p- and q-values but as(methylDiff, "Granges") only the q-value.

Thanks,
Heidi
